companyDescription: eVTOL air-taxi developer nearing FAA type certification — recently acquired Boeing's Wisk Aero (autonomous) and Insitu (drone) units to broaden its aerospace platform
priceNote: 52-week range $4.30-$14.62; near the low end, down ~35% YTD on cash-burn concerns
summary: Archer reports Q3 2026 earnings in the Nov 5-9, 2026 window (not yet officially confirmed to the exact day). The setup follows a Q2 2026 print where revenue surged 213% YoY to $5M and the Wisk Aero + Insitu acquisitions were announced, driving a standalone +15% pop, while the earnings reaction itself was muted (~-1%) amid sector-wide headline noise. Consensus target $11.63 (67% Buy) implies +107.3% upside from $5.61 — the largest upside in this batch, reflecting how far the stock has fallen (-35% YTD) versus a Street that hasn't fully cut targets. Base case (+45%) assumes reaffirmed certification progress and is well above the lane's realized 14d P75 of +6.6% — the gap is a multi-quarter re-rating horizon toward FAA type certification, not near-term optimism bias, and the specific driver is a certification-timeline update, not the Q3 numbers alone.

catalysts.name: Q3 2026 Earnings + Certification Update
catalysts.description: Estimated Nov 5-9, 2026 (exact day not yet company-confirmed). Watch for FAA type-certification timeline commentary alongside the numbers — Archer closed Phase 3 of the FAA's 4-phase process in May 2026 and 'late 2026' final issuance is the Street's working assumption, not a hard date.

risks: Pre-revenue on the core eVTOL program — Q2 2026 revenue was just $5M; the investment case is almost entirely certification-timeline dependent, not current financials
FAA full type-certification has already slipped multiple times industry-wide; 'late 2026' is the Street's assumption, not a company-committed date — some analysts model mid-2027 or later
Cash burn is heavy; further dilution into 2027 is a real risk despite the balance-sheet boost from the Wisk/Insitu deal
eVTOL sector sentiment is highly correlated to Joby Aviation — a Joby-specific setback can drag ACHR even without ACHR-specific news
Exact Q3 earnings date is not yet company-confirmed (estimated window only) — provenance is weaker than the other picks in this batch

estimateDates.note: Estimated window Nov 5-9; not yet officially confirmed

macroRisk.rateOutlook: Fed hiked to 3.75-4.00% on Sep 16, 2026 (first hike since 2023); next FOMC is Oct 27-28, 2026 — just days before ACHR's estimated Q3 window, adding a macro wildcard on top of an already fuzzy earnings date.
macroRisk.inflationNote: The hike is inflation-driven; pre-revenue, heavy-cash-burn names like Archer are the most exposed cohort to a higher discount rate and tighter access to the capital markets it will eventually need again.
macroRisk.sectorImpact: eVTOL names are down sharply in 2026 (ACHR -35% YTD) on cash-burn and certification-delay concerns; a hawkish Fed compounds the multiple compression already underway rather than being the primary driver.
macroRisk.summary: HIGH macro risk — Archer is pre-revenue and cash-burning in a renewed hiking cycle; the certification-timeline catalyst is largely company/regulator-specific, but financing risk is real if the timeline slips again.
